scope: Controlled production-browser MKV-to-MP4 direct-destination buffer/core comparison

environment.command: WITHIN_RUN_COUNT=3 WITHIN_DESTINATION_MODE=direct-handle npm run profile:memory -- test.mkv mkv-to-mp4 fixtures/media/test-mkv.manifest.json

acceptance.primaryMemoryFormula: peak complete Chromium process-tree private memory during conversion - stable clean blank-Chromium process-tree private memory
acceptance.requiredValidation: Full output SHA-256, independent media validation, repeatability, bounded I/O, and cleanup recovery

rejected.name: 256 KiB standard-remux core on the same direct destination
rejected.temporaryChange: workers/conversion.worker.ts selected MAX_WRITE_CHUNK instead of DIRECT_REMUX_WRITE_CHUNK for direct MKV-to-MP4
rejected.rejectionReason: It preserved correctness and used less process memory, but its median elapsed time was 16.40385071404393% longer than the retained specialist.

comparison.decision: Retain the 1 MiB direct-remux specialist because it is the fastest compliant candidate in this controlled current-build A/B.

historicalContext.interpretation: This older result is faster, but it used a different Chrome version and an older engine output/build, so it is not an isolated candidate comparison. The current A/B changes only the core selector; investigation of the historical build/browser regression remains part of P-08.

tenGiBClarification.clarification: The approximately 210 MiB figure is incremental private memory, not output size. The genuine browser remux output was 10,746,764,442 bytes and was independently validated before deletion.

retainedArtifacts: the accepted raw report triplet under outputs/reports
